findings.title: `isAccessTokenId` returns false when the grant shortcut matches, so the check is inverted
findings.description: The guard `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` has its condition inverted. It rejects exactly the token IDs that carry the expected grant and accepts the ones that don't. Every `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectAuthReqIdToToken` and device-flow assertion that uses this matcher is therefore checking the opposite of what its name and message say. The fix is to negate the condition (`!...equals(...)`) once the index is also corrected (see the next finding).

findings.title: Grant shortcut is read from the wrong character offset in `isAccessTokenId`
findings.description: The token ID format is `sstt gg:uuid`, where session type occupies 0-based chars 0–1, token type 2–3, and grant shortcut 4–5. The helper uses `substring(3, 5)`, which captures the last char of the token type plus the first char of the grant shortcut. The comment says the shortcut "starts at character 4th char", which describes 1-based position 4, not 0-based index 4 as the code assumes. The correct slice is `substring(4, 6)`.

findings.title: Constructor null-checks `grantType` twice and never checks `rawTokenId`
findings.description: The last two `Objects.requireNonNull` calls in the constructor both pass `grantType`. The second one's message says "Null rawTokenId not allowed", so the intended check is on `rawTokenId`. As written, a null raw token ID is accepted and can be encoded into the token ID string as `"null"` by `encodeTokenId`.
